questions.question: Who was the revenue minister of Akbar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Todar Mal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Todar Mal** was the **Finance Minister** or Revenue Minister in the court of **Mughal Emperor Akbar**. He is renowned for his administrative and revenue reforms.
 
• He introduced the **Zabt system**, which is considered one of the most systematic land revenue systems in Indian history. This system ensured uniformity and fairness in tax collection.
 
• Todar Mal played a key role in the implementation of the **land survey and measurement system**. This involved dividing agricultural land into units based on productivity and fixing revenue rates accordingly.
 
• He standardized the revenue collection process, ensuring that farmers were not exploited by local officials. The revenue was collected in cash or kind depending on the region's agricultural produce.
 
• The reforms introduced by Todar Mal under Akbar's administration greatly enhanced the efficiency of the empire's financial system, contributing significantly to the prosperity of the Mughal Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zabt System:**

 
 
• Under Todar Mal's guidance, the **Zabt system** was implemented, which calculated revenue based on the measured productivity of the land. This system was used in areas where agricultural output was uniform and predictable.
 
• Land was categorized into **three types**: Polaj (cultivated annually), Parauti (cultivated intermittently), and Chachar (cultivated after long intervals).
 
• The system ensured accurate measurement of land and proper documentation of land ownership and revenue liabilities.
 
 
 
• **Akbar's Administrative Reforms:**
 
 
• Akbar introduced several administrative reforms to centralize and strengthen the Mughal Empire. Todar Mal's revenue reforms were a cornerstone of this effort.
 
• The administrative system was divided into **provinces or Subahs**, each headed by a governor, ensuring efficient governance and tax collection.
 
 
 
• **Other Ministers in Akbar's Court:**
 
 
• **Birbal:** Known for his wit and intelligence, Birbal was one of the nine jewels (Navratnas) in Akbar’s court. He advised Akbar on matters of diplomacy and cultural integration.
 
• **Raja Man Singh:** A trusted general and statesman, Raja Man Singh was instrumental in expanding Akbar's empire through military conquests.
 
• **Raja Bharmal:** Raja Bharmal was the father of Akbar's wife, Jodha Bai, and played a role in establishing alliances between the Mughal Empire and Rajput states.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Todar Mal's Reforms:**
 
 
• The revenue system introduced by Todar Mal served as a model for subsequent rulers in India, including the British colonial administration.
 
• It emphasized transparency, accountability, and fairness, which reduced corruption and exploitation in the collection of taxes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Revenue Systems:**

 
 
• The Zabt system was based on accurate measurement and documentation, unlike earlier systems that relied on arbitrary assessments.
 
• It laid the foundation for modern revenue systems and inspired the British Revenue Settlement during their rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Historical Legacy:**
 
 
• Todar Mal's reforms are considered a landmark in the history of Indian administration. His contribution to Akbar’s reign established a legacy of efficient governance.
 
• His reforms ensured that peasants were not burdened unnecessarily, and the state received consistent revenue, fostering economic stability.

questions.question: Who wrote 'The Jungle Book' in 1894?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudyard Kipling**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'The Jungle Book'** was written by **Rudyard Kipling** and published in the year **1894**.
 
• The book is a collection of stories, featuring the adventures of **Mowgli**, a human child raised by wolves in the jungle.
 
• Rudyard Kipling was born on **30th December 1865** in **Bombay (now Mumbai), India**, and is known for his works that explore themes of British colonialism.
 
• Kipling’s mastery in storytelling brought to life the rich fauna of the Indian jungle, such as **Bagheera (the panther), Baloo (the bear), and Shere Khan (the tiger)**.
 
• The book is widely regarded as a classic of children’s literature and has been adapted into numerous films, plays, and animations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rudyard Kipling**:

 
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Literature** in **1907**, making him the youngest recipient of the prize at the time.
 
• His other famous works include **'Kim'**, **'The Man Who Would Be King'**, and poems like **'If—'** and **'Gunga Din'**.
 
• Kipling's writing style is characterized by vivid descriptions, moral lessons, and the integration of British imperial themes.
 
 
 
• **About 'The Jungle Book'**:
 
 
• The book contains a total of **seven stories**, many of which revolve around Mowgli, while some feature other characters like **Rikki-Tikki-Tavi**, a brave mongoose.
 
• It explores themes such as the importance of **family, loyalty, and identity**.
 
• The "Law of the Jungle" is a recurring motif, symbolizing rules and ethics in a complex society.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **William Shakespeare**: He was a famous English playwright and poet from the Elizabethan era, known for works like **'Hamlet'**, **'Macbeth'**, and **'Romeo and Juliet'**. He did not write 'The Jungle Book'.
 
• **Stephen Alter**: An Indian-American author known for books on Himalayan ecology and culture, but he is not connected to 'The Jungle Book'.
 
• **Edgar Allan Poe**: An American writer famous for his gothic tales and poems such as **'The Raven'** and **'The Tell-Tale Heart'**. He did not write 'The Jungle Book'.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inspiration for 'The Jungle Book'**: Kipling was inspired by his childhood in India, particularly the wildlife and culture he observed.
 
• **Legacy**: Disney adapted 'The Jungle Book' into an animated movie in **1967**, and a live-action remake was released in **2016**.
 
• **Impact**: The book has been used as a teaching tool for children to understand moral values and the importance of coexistence with nature.

questions.question: How many authors are to be selected under the PM-YUVA 3.0?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PM-YUVA 3.0** (Pradhan Mantri Yuva Utsav) is the third edition of the scheme, aimed at promoting young authors in India.
 
• The initiative is part of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which emphasizes fostering critical thinking, creativity, and writing skills among youth.
 
• A total of **50 authors** will be selected under this program to encourage young talent in the literary field.
 
• The selected authors will be provided with training and mentorship to develop their literary works, which will also be published.
 
• This program is targeted at **Indian citizens aged 30 and below**, ensuring a focus on nurturing young talent across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Theme of PM-YUVA 3.0:**

 
 
• The theme for this edition is centered around **Indian culture, heritage, and vision for the future**.
 
• The focus is to create a platform for **young voices** to articulate the rich diversity and traditions of India.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• Applicants must be **Indian citizens** aged 30 years or younger.
 
• They should submit a manuscript or concept note for consideration.
 
 
 
• **Benefits for Selected Authors:**
 
 
• The selected participants will receive **mentorship** from renowned authors and literary experts.
 
• Their works will be **published and promoted** by the Government of India.
 
• A **financial grant** will be provided for the development of their manuscripts.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The program is being managed by the **National Book Trust (NBT), India**.
 
• It aligns with the vision of the **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav** celebrations to commemorate 75 years of India’s independence.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• It aims to **cultivate new literary talent** in India and promote reading and writing habits among the youth.
 
• The initiative also helps in fostering a greater appreciation of India’s **culture and heritage**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Previous Editions:**

 
 
• **PM-YUVA 1.0** and **2.0** focused on identifying young talent and publishing their works across various genres.
 
• These editions also emphasized inculcating the habit of reading and promoting intellectual growth among youth.
 
 
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**
 
 
• The policy underlines the importance of **creative expression** and the development of critical thinking.
 
• It supports programs like PM-YUVA to align with its vision of fostering **holistic learning**.
 
 
 
• **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav:**
 
 
• This initiative is part of the Government of India’s celebrations to mark **75 years of independence**.
 
• It aims to showcase India’s rich heritage, achievements, and aspirations for the future.

questions.question: How many sections does the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**358**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023** is a significant legal document introduced to replace the colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860.
 
• The BNS comprises a total of **358 sections**, which aim to modernize and restructure India's criminal justice system to meet contemporary needs.
 
• The new legislation emphasizes the principles of justice, fairness, and equality while addressing issues with the older IPC that were deemed outdated or inadequate.
 
• The **Government of India** introduced this bill as part of broader reforms in criminal laws, including changes to the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) and the Evidence Act.
 
• The BNS incorporates provisions for stricter punishments for crimes such as terrorism, organized crime, and crimes against women and children, reflecting the evolving socio-political landscape of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Purpose of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS):**

 
 
• The BNS aims to replace the outdated Indian Penal Code, ensuring that legal provisions align with **modern societal values** and international standards.
 
• It emphasizes a victim-centric approach, ensuring justice for victims of crime while safeguarding the rights of the accused.
 
• Clearer definitions of offenses and the inclusion of new categories of crimes address gaps in the previous legal framework.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Reform:**
 
 
• The IPC was drafted during the British colonial era and reflected the priorities of that time. The BNS seeks to address the **present-day needs of Indian society**.
 
• It incorporates provisions for crimes like **cybercrimes, financial frauds, and human trafficking**, which were not adequately addressed in the IPC.
 
• The legislation also aims to expedite the legal process, reducing delays in the criminal justice system.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with the Indian Penal Code (IPC):**
 
 
• The IPC had a total of **511 sections**, compared to the BNS’s **358 sections**, reflecting efforts to streamline and simplify the legal framework.
 
• The BNS eliminates provisions considered obsolete or redundant while introducing new sections for crimes relevant to modern times.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Justice Delivery:**
 
 
• The BNS promotes **alternative dispute resolution mechanisms** and community policing to reduce the burden on courts.
 
• Provisions for stricter penalties and reforms in sentencing aim to deter crimes and ensure proportional justice.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of BNS:**
 
 
• Inclusion of provisions for **gender equality** and protection of marginalized communities.
 
• Focus on reducing delays through technology-driven solutions like online filing of complaints and virtual court hearings.
 
• Enhanced safeguards against misuse of laws, ensuring a balance between enforcement and individual rights.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Introduction of the Bill:** The BNS, along with two other bills aimed at reforming criminal laws, was introduced in **August 2023** by the Union Home Minister.
 
• **Scope of Reforms:** The reforms aim to address not just substantive criminal law but also procedural aspects, ensuring a **comprehensive overhaul** of the criminal justice system.
 
• **Public Participation:** The government sought feedback from various stakeholders, including legal experts and the general public, to make the reforms inclusive and representative.
 
• **Implementation Challenges:** The transition from the IPC to the BNS requires extensive training for law enforcement agencies and judiciary members.

questions.question: Strokes, Starts and Turns are some of the Techniques of which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swimming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Strokes, Starts, and Turns** are essential techniques in the sport of **Swimming**. These are fundamental skills used by swimmers to achieve maximum efficiency and speed in water.
 
• **Strokes**: Swimming involves various strokes such as **freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly**. Each stroke has unique movements and techniques designed to optimize propulsion and minimize drag.
 
• **Starts**: Swimmers must execute powerful starts, often from a diving block, to enter the water quickly and begin their race effectively. The start technique includes a strong push-off and streamlined body position.
 
• **Turns**: In competitive swimming, turns are crucial for maintaining speed during transitions at the end of a lap. Techniques like the **flip turn** and **open turn** are commonly used, depending on the stroke.
 
• These techniques are refined through rigorous training and are essential for competitive swimming events like the **Olympics**, **World Championships**, and other international competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Swimming as a Sport:**

 
 
• Swimming has been a part of the **Olympic Games** since **1896**. It is one of the most popular and physically demanding sports worldwide.
 
• Competitive swimming includes events like **sprints** (50m, 100m), **middle-distance** (200m, 400m), and **long-distance** (800m, 1500m).
 
• Relay events such as the **4x100m freestyle relay** involve teams competing together.
 
• Swimming competitions occur in two types of pools: **short course (25m)** and **long course (50m)**.
 
 
 
• **Techniques in Swimming:**
 
 
• **Freestyle:** The most common and fastest stroke, involving alternate arm movements and flutter kicks.
 
• **Backstroke:** Swimmers float on their backs, moving arms in a circular motion and performing flutter kicks.
 
• **Breaststroke:** A slower stroke that requires simultaneous arm movements and frog-like kicks.
 
• **Butterfly:** A challenging stroke requiring both arms to move simultaneously in a circular motion, accompanied by dolphin kicks.
 
• **Starts and Turns:** Athletes train to perform explosive starts and efficient turns to save time and maintain momentum.
 
 
 
• **Physical Benefits of Swimming:**
 
 
• Swimming improves **cardiovascular health**, **muscle strength**, and **flexibility**.
 
• It is a low-impact activity suitable for individuals of all ages, as it reduces stress on joints.
 
• Swimming enhances **lung capacity** and promotes overall endurance and stamina.
 
 
 
• **Interesting Facts:**
 
 
• Michael Phelps, an American swimmer, is the most decorated Olympian of all time with **28 medals**, including **23 golds**.
 
• Famous swimming events include the **FINA World Championships** and **Commonwealth Games**.
 
• Swimmers utilize specialized gear like **swim caps**, **goggles**, and **competitive swimsuits** to enhance performance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Sports:**

 
 
• **Baseball:** Focuses on hitting, pitching, and fielding; has no relation to swimming techniques.
 
• **Golf:** Requires precision in swinging and putting; unrelated to water-based activities.
 
• **Badminton:** Involves shuttlecock handling and racket skills; entirely different from swimming.
 
 
 
• **Training and Coaching:**
 
 
• Professional swimming training involves **regular practice**, **strength conditioning**, and **diet monitoring**.
 
• Coaches analyze swimmers' techniques to improve their **stroke efficiency** and **speed**.

questions.question: To protect one-horned rhinos from poachers which state has launched the Operation Falcon in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Falcon** was launched by the state of **Assam** in **August 2025** to protect the **one-horned rhinos**, a species that is critically endangered and endemic to the Indian subcontinent. 
 
• **Assam** is home to the **Kaziranga National Park**, which is globally renowned for its population of one-horned rhinos and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The initiative aims to combat **poaching activities** that threaten the survival of this iconic species. Poachers target these rhinos primarily for their horns, which are highly valued in illegal wildlife markets.
 
• **Operation Falcon** involves multiple stakeholders, including local government agencies, forest officials, wildlife experts, and law enforcement authorities, to ensure the comprehensive protection of rhinos.
 
• Assam's government has also employed advanced technologies such as **drone surveillance**, **GPS tracking**, and **anti-poaching camps** under Operation Falcon to strengthen conservation efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **One-Horned Rhinos:**

 
 
• The **Indian rhinoceros**, commonly known as the one-horned rhinoceros, is primarily found in northeastern India and Nepal.
 
• It is listed as **vulnerable** on the **IUCN Red List**, with Assam being one of its last remaining habitats.
 
• Rhino horns are composed of **keratin**, the same protein that makes up human nails and hair, and are falsely believed to have medicinal properties, driving illegal trade.
 
 
 
• **Kaziranga National Park:**
 
 
• Located in **Assam**, Kaziranga National Park is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and a critical habitat for one-horned rhinos.
 
• The park is renowned for its **success in rhino conservation**, housing approximately **2,400 rhinos** as per recent census data.
 
• Kaziranga also supports a wide range of biodiversity, including species like tigers, elephants, swamp deer, and wild water buffalo.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Poaching Measures:**
 
 
• Over the years, Assam has intensified its **anti-poaching efforts** by forming **dedicated task forces**, establishing **anti-poaching camps**, and adopting modern technologies like drones and thermal imaging cameras.
 
• Local communities are actively involved in conservation efforts, providing surveillance and reporting suspicious activities.
 
• International collaborations, such as partnerships with the **WWF** and **TRAFFIC**, have further supported rhino protection.
 
 
 
• **Other Rhino Habitats in India:**
 
 
• Besides Assam, one-horned rhinos are found in **Manas National Park**, **Orang National Park**, and **Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary**.
 
• Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary has one of the highest densities of rhinos in India despite being much smaller in size compared to Kaziranga.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rhino Census:** Assam conducts periodic rhino censuses to monitor population trends and assess the success of conservation efforts.
 
• **Kaziranga National Park Floods:** The park faces annual floods due to the Brahmaputra River, which impacts wildlife but also regenerates the ecosystem.
 
• **Global Rhino Conservation:** International efforts, including the **Rhino Impact Bond** and campaigns by **Save the Rhino International**, contribute to rhino protection worldwide.
 
• **Rhino Conservation Challenges:** Key challenges include habitat loss, human-wildlife conflict, and the growing demand for rhino horns in Asian markets.

questions.question: The diameter of the bamboo flutes is usually about ______ cm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.9 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The diameter of bamboo flutes is generally around **1.9 cm**, which makes them ideal for producing the desired sound and tonal quality.
 
• Bamboo flutes are known for their simplicity and natural acoustic properties, which are influenced significantly by their diameter and length.
 
• The **1.9 cm diameter** ensures that the airflow and resonance inside the flute create the right musical notes without distortion.
 
• Flutes with this diameter are easier to handle and are widely used by beginners and professionals alike due to their precision in sound production.
 
• Choosing the right diameter is crucial as it affects the pitch, tone, and ease of playing the instrument. A flute of **1.9 cm diameter** meets these criteria effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bamboo Flutes:**

 
 
• Bamboo flutes are among the oldest musical instruments and are found in various cultures worldwide.
 
• They are traditionally made from a single piece of bamboo and have finger holes for controlling the pitch and notes.
 
• The length and diameter of the flute are critical in determining the type of sound it produces.
 
• Shorter flutes with smaller diameters produce higher-pitched sounds, whereas longer ones with larger diameters produce deeper and mellower tones.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Diameter in Flutes:**
 
 
• The diameter directly impacts the sound waves and resonance inside the flute, which in turn affects the pitch and tone.
 
• For bamboo flutes, a diameter of around **1.9 cm** is ideal for achieving a balance between ease of use and sound quality.
 
• Larger diameters may produce deeper tones but are harder to play, while smaller ones may lead to sharper and higher pitches.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Bamboo Flutes:**
 
 
• Bamboo flutes are commonly used in traditional and classical music forms in countries like **India, China, and Japan**.
 
• In Indian music, the bamboo flute is an integral part of both Hindustani and Carnatic classical music traditions.
 
• They are also used in meditation and relaxation music due to their soothing and natural sound.
 
 
 
• **Other Flute Variations:**
 
 
• Western flutes are usually made of metal and have a different diameter and mechanism compared to bamboo flutes.
 
• Fipple flutes, such as recorders, have a different construction and are primarily used in Western classical and folk music.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Material:** Bamboo is preferred for its lightweight, durability, and natural acoustic qualities.
 
• **Historical Use:** Bamboo flutes have been used for centuries in cultures worldwide, symbolizing simplicity and spiritual harmony.
 
• **Variants:** Other than 1.9 cm diameter flutes, variations exist to suit different musical needs and preferences.
 
• **Maintenance:** Bamboo flutes require proper care to avoid cracks and preserve their tonal quality over time.

questions.question: What were the cities of the Indus Valley generally enclosed with?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fortified walls with gateways**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The cities of the **Indus Valley Civilization** were generally enclosed with **fortified walls** that included gateways, indicating a focus on urban planning and security.
 
• The fortified walls served multiple purposes such as **defense against potential invasions**, protection against floods, and demarcation of the city’s boundaries.
 
• These walls were constructed using baked bricks of uniform size, showcasing the **advanced engineering skills** and **standardization** techniques of the Indus Valley people.
 
• Prominent cities like **Harappa**, **Mohenjo-Daro**, and **Kalibangan** were known for having these fortified structures, which often separated the **citadel** (upper town) from the lower residential area.
 
• The gateways in the walls were used not only for entry and exit but also for **trade, taxation, and monitoring movement**. This highlights the economic and administrative sophistication of the civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization:**

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization (2600-1900 BCE) is one of the world’s oldest urban civilizations, thriving in areas of present-day **India and Pakistan**.
 
• It is renowned for its **meticulous urban planning**, with well-laid streets, drainage systems, and large public baths.
 
• Key cities include **Harappa** (Punjab, Pakistan), **Mohenjo-Daro** (Sindh, Pakistan), and **Dholavira** (Gujarat, India).
 
 
 
• **Construction Techniques:**
 
 
• The walls were primarily made of **baked bricks**, a notable feature distinguishing the Indus Valley Civilization from other contemporary civilizations.
 
• The use of standardized brick sizes suggests a centralized authority overseeing construction practices.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of Fortified Walls:**
 
 
• **Defense:** The walls protected the inhabitants from invaders and natural calamities like floods.
 
• **Urban Organization:** The walls demarcated administrative areas (citadel) from residential ones, reflecting a hierarchical society.
 
• **Trade Control:** The gateways in the walls allowed for regulation of trade and collection of taxes.
 
 
 
• **Other Features of Indus Valley Cities:**
 
 
• Advanced drainage systems with covered drains and soak pits indicate a focus on hygiene and sanitation.
 
• Public buildings, granaries, and baths like the **Great Bath of Mohenjo-Daro** highlight the civilization’s architectural achievements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: Wooden fences**

 
 
• Wooden fences were not a feature of Indus Valley cities. Wood was primarily used for making tools, carts, and furniture rather than for constructing large structures.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Stone barricades**
 
 
• Stone was rarely used in Indus construction. Baked bricks were the dominant material, reflecting the availability of resources like clay in the region.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Moats and drawbridges**
 
 
• While moats and drawbridges were common in medieval forts, there is no archaeological evidence of such structures in Indus Valley cities.
 
 
 
• Indus Valley’s focus on fortified walls with gateways was a unique feature of its urban planning, serving both practical and administrative purposes.

questions.question: The International Space Station circles Earth roughly ______ times a day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** orbits the Earth at an average altitude of approximately **408 kilometers (253 miles)**.
 
• It completes one orbit around the Earth in approximately **90 minutes**, traveling at a speed of around **28,000 kilometers per hour (17,500 miles per hour)**.
 
• Due to its orbital speed and duration, the ISS circles the Earth about **16 times a day**, providing astronauts the chance to witness 16 sunrises and sunsets daily.
 
• The specific orbital mechanics of the ISS ensure that it maintains a low Earth orbit, allowing it to remain in continuous motion around the Earth.
 
• This frequency of orbit facilitates various scientific experiments and observations, as the ISS provides multiple views of the Earth’s surface in a single day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of the ISS:**

 
 
• The ISS is a joint project involving **NASA** (United States), **Roscosmos** (Russia), **ESA** (European Space Agency), **JAXA** (Japan), and **CSA** (Canada).
 
• It serves as a unique microgravity laboratory, enabling scientists to conduct experiments in biology, physics, astronomy, and other fields that require the absence of gravity.
 
• The ISS has been continuously occupied since **November 2000**, making it one of the longest-running human spaceflight missions in history.
 
• The station is modular, with components such as living quarters, laboratories, and storage units assembled in orbit since its launch in **1998**.
 
• The ISS weighs approximately **420,000 kilograms (925,000 pounds)** and spans the size of a football field, making it the largest human-made structure in space.
 
 
 
• **Orbital Mechanics:**
 
 
• The ISS orbits in a **low Earth orbit (LEO)**, which ranges between **180 and 2,000 kilometers (111–1,243 miles)** above the Earth's surface.
 
• Its orbit is inclined at an angle of **51.6 degrees** to the equator, allowing it to cover most of the Earth's populated areas.
 
• The speed and altitude of the ISS are carefully maintained to counteract atmospheric drag and gravitational forces, ensuring it stays in orbit.
 
• Occasional adjustments, known as **reboosts**, are performed using onboard thrusters or visiting spacecraft to maintain its altitude.
 
 
 
• **Astronauts’ Perspective:**
 
 
• Due to the ISS’s frequent orbits, astronauts experience 16 sunrises and sunsets daily, providing a unique perspective on Earth’s atmosphere and weather patterns.
 
• The rapid orbital motion enables the station to pass over different continents multiple times in a single day, enhancing global observational capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Contribution:**
 
 
• The ISS enables groundbreaking research in areas like **medicine**, **climate change**, and **materials science**.
 
• It acts as a testing ground for technologies that will support future human exploration missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

questions.question: Which religious community had the second-largest population in India as per Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muslim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Census 2011** of India recorded the population distribution among various religious communities.
 
• As per the census, the **Hindu community** had the largest population, constituting approximately **79.8%** of India's total population.
 
• The **Muslim community** was identified as the second-largest religious group, accounting for around **14.2%** of the population.
 
• Other religious communities such as **Christians (2.3%)**, **Sikhs (1.7%)**, **Buddhists (0.7%)**, and **Jains (0.4%)** had smaller proportions in comparison.
 
• The significant Muslim population in India is concentrated in states like **Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Maharashtra, and Kerala**, among others.

• The **Census of India** is conducted every 10 years to collect comprehensive demographic data.
 
• The **2011 Census** was the 15th national census conducted since 1872.
 
• It provided detailed insights into India's **population, literacy rate, sex ratio, urban-rural distribution**, and religious composition.
 
• India's total population as per the 2011 Census was approximately **1.21 billion**.
 
 
 
• **Muslim Population in India:**
 
 
• India is home to the **third-largest Muslim population** in the world, after Indonesia and Pakistan.
 
• Muslims in India are predominantly Sunni, with a smaller proportion of Shia Muslims.
 
• Significant Muslim-majority areas include **Kashmir** and regions in **Kerala**.

• **Jains:** Representing **0.4%**, they are concentrated in states like **Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: The philosophical concept that everything in the universe is one divine essence is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahman** is a key concept in Hindu philosophy, representing the ultimate reality or the divine essence that permeates everything in the universe.
 
• It is described as the eternal, unchanging, infinite, and formless reality, which is the source and foundation of all existence.
 
• In the **Upanishads**, Brahman is often discussed as the ultimate truth that transcends the physical world and is beyond human comprehension.
 
• The concept of Brahman is closely connected to the idea of **Atman**, which refers to the individual soul. Hindu philosophy often emphasizes the unity of Atman and Brahman, signifying the connection between the self and the universal reality.
 
• This philosophical idea is a central theme in **Advaita Vedanta**, a prominent school of Hindu philosophy, which teaches that there is no distinction between Brahman and Atman.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Samiti:**

 
 
• Samiti is a term used in ancient Indian history to refer to an assembly or gathering, often for decision-making purposes.
 
• It is not related to the philosophical concept of divine essence but is significant in the context of governance and social organization in ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Yajna:**
 
 
• Yajna refers to a ritual sacrifice performed in Vedic traditions, involving offerings made to deities through fire.
 
• It symbolizes the idea of reciprocity between humans and the divine but does not represent the concept of the universe being one divine essence.
 
 
 
• **Purandar:**
 
 
• Purandar is a name associated with the Hindu deity Indra, the king of gods in Vedic mythology.
 
• It does not align with the philosophical idea of Brahman, which signifies a universal divine essence rather than a specific deity.
 
 
 
• **Brahman:**
 
 
• The concept of Brahman is foundational in Hinduism and is discussed extensively in sacred texts such as the **Upanishads** and the **Bhagavad Gita**.
 
• It is often described as the supreme cosmic spirit or consciousness that is both immanent and transcendent.
 
• Philosophical schools like **Advaita Vedanta** interpret Brahman as non-dual, suggesting that the ultimate reality is undivided and singular.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Upanishads:**

 
 
• These ancient texts are philosophical treatises that explore the nature of reality, self, and the universe.
 
• The concept of Brahman is central in these texts, often described as the ultimate truth and reality.
 
 
 
• **Advaita Vedanta:**
 
 
• This school of philosophy advocates the non-duality of Brahman and Atman, asserting that there is no distinction between the individual soul and the universal essence.
 
• It was profoundly developed by **Adi Shankaracharya**, a key figure in Indian philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Vedic Texts:**
 
 
• While the early Vedic texts primarily focus on rituals and deities, the later texts like Upanishads delve deeper into metaphysical concepts such as Brahman.
 
• These texts form the basis of much of Hindu philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The understanding of Brahman influences not only religious practices but also philosophical inquiries into the nature of existence, consciousness, and the universe.
 
• It serves as a unifying principle in Hindu thought, connecting diverse beliefs and practices.
